correctness.rationale: For probability Haar measure and ordinary trace characters, Schur orthogonality gives the stated L² denominator. Clebsch–Gordan and orthogonality count triangles of integer indices. In a cube of side m+1 the three violation sets are disjoint, each of size binom(m+2,3); the two unequal boxes are obtained by adding or deleting a single layer requiring i+j≥n+1, giving n(n+1)/2 and (n+2)(n+3)/2 respectively. This includes n=0. Only even powers of each character contribute by central parity, and cubing |aχ_n+bχ_{n+1}|² gives 3+12 cos²φ for both mixed weights. The upward-opening derivative is positive at 0 and negative at both 1/2 and 1, yielding a unique maximum in (0,1/2) and real relative phase at equality. Factoring the cubic about its critical point gives the claimed Q_n; in fact x+2x_n<2 on [0,1], giving Q_n>6n³+24n²+27n+8. Its slope is negative and x=1 has zero phase loss, proving sharpness of Q_n(1). At x=1/2 the first two derivatives have leading terms −3n² and −12n³; the unique maximizer converges to 1/2 by uniform convergence of n⁻³P_n. Taylor expansion gives −1/(4n) displacement to first order. At 1/2 the value is 2n³+9n²+O(n); optimizing changes it by O(n). These are analytic checks of the all-index claim; the supplied quadrature and finite tensor-product checker were inspected, not run.
residual_risks: No formal verification claimed; sharpness of c_n concerns the squared mass-coordinate deficit, not a distance in the full complex coefficient space.
